Can see this dropping over time, honestly. Right now I’m carried by how great Inde is here (the rest of the acting is, by and large, mediocre) and the boldness. But the theming here gets pretty sloppy even with the simple premise. The film does a good enough job making Bear out to be “the bad guy” for the most part. He’s meek, cowardly, selfish, and irresponsible, to the extent that he is clearly a rapist by the film’s end. I think where I get a little frustrated with how clumsy the messaging here is, is that because the premise is still fantastical by nature, there’s still that lingering aspect of plausible deniability for too much of the film. Bear thinks it’s odd at first and he wonders if it worked (looks it up and originally the info actually suggests it DOESN’T work) but rolls with it. And initially he tries to be respectful in the face of odd behavior. And eventually he starts rolling with it. By the time it’s really confirmed for him, he’s ebbing between whether to kill himself to set her free and not caring about Nikki or her autonomy at all as long as wish Nikki can “perform” Nikki appropriately. The former would be near heroic and the other is downright monstrous. Everything is unequivocally Bear’s fault (though Ian certainly isn’t helpful) and yet the situation is so outrageous that the character’s condemnation accidentally becomes somewhat conditional. Unlike in the real world, Bear is never given a choice to just respect Nikki’s autonomy after the wish is made, before he begins to act intentionally. He immediately is locked into suicide or manipulation as his two options, and that’s where this basically fails as cultural critique. Technically there’s possibly a loophole with the wish and he actually attempts to exploit this, but there’s no clear indication as to how it would’ve panned out. The inherent issue here is that as pathetic as Bear is, there is probably a version of this film that gives him more reasonable opportunities to exit this situation cleanly and he still doesn’t take them due to his desire to possess “Nikki.” But that’s not really this movie and the messaging gets confused as a result. This thing is also very, very mean-spirited in general. I don’t really expect horror to be happy, but this whole thing really doesn’t have me rooting for anyone to make it through unscathed. I’m not sure any of the core four here totally deserves their fate, but I also think it’s telling that the two men are far closer to deserving it and the women go through, far, far worse, to the point of borderline directorial cruelty when they’ve functionally done very little wrong. Nikki is clearly the primary victim here and thinking about the film and how flimsy its messaging is, this reveals itself to be nearly torture porn for violence against women. I think about how easy Ian gets off, and maybe that’s “commentary,” but when I see interviews with Barker, he seems wholly unable to articulate any sort of genuine thematic intent. I think he just understands that watching women suffer feels bad, and decided to make that a movie. He’s right, but that doesn’t make this any good. The more I write this, the more I realize I do not like Obsession.

Inde Navarrette's spectacular performance reminded me of a golden retriever (it's important her performance is natural at the beginning and then as a stunted dog later) and I found myself think about why I'd never own a pet again. There is this perverted want from the owner to own a dog. It is captivity. Moreover the dog doesn't have a choice in loving who will ultimately feed them. While you live your life, their life is nearly paused (you should take them to a dog daycare) and you restrict what they can do when you're together. It's this weird, acceptable relationship where almost instantly you can be loved. Just because you chose this for her doesn't make it less real. It sounds to me you have a moral obligation to be there for her. But love is not meant to be instant. It's not even meant to be initially comfortable or gratifying. OBSESSION, which I don't really think is the right title, could be sold as the anti-Prince Charming and Disney fantasy. Horror elements are clearly inspired by the Forbidden Room scene in PULSE. What's actually provocative isn't a gun in a person's mouth but expecting the bullet to come as they fumble with the mechanics of killing themselves. I had just told Tony the other day I don't reflect anymore (I suspect because I'm just so focused now) then I put on Depression Cherry and listened to it three times on the plane to Spain. Levitation's lyrics "there is no right time" and Days of Candy's "the universe is riding off with you" just hit me. I think I realized after watching OBSESSION, which iterates on skipping the awkward asking part of starting a relationship, how I'd been keeping myself in limbo and protecting myself from any possibility for a little too long. I start thinking of apologizing to Ines 20 years ago for leaving her in the basement and having ignored it, I think I thought it was weird kissing a girl younger than me at the time, that you were supposed to kiss someone your own age. I lost a friend when she moved. I thought about Kat and writing back after she ghosted me for two years but I was probably coming up on my own anniversary. I thought about how Nate was someone I felt close to but never really made a strong enough effort to maintain that relationship (so I texted him). I thought about, again, how I need to be kinder to my dad. That being disappointed is not an excuse for being irritable or curt. I thought about getting a plane ticket to Biaritz. I thought about the four or so questions I want to ask this girl at the gym and how this past week would have been a good time to ask them but I skipped lifting because my elbows and wrist hurt but then asking those questions would have been fine to ask the last two years and next week too. I thought about how I feel like the ground underneath me is unstable, how I can't take a shower without feeling like the tub might split in half and I'd sink through the floor or how some parts of the house feel like I could put a leg through it if I jumped. I thought about how these coming months feel like a major infection point in my life where I've been riding on table stakes with this game and either the last five months of development and time and sacrifice (no one but me asked to do)—well, I'll be rich or I'll have been delusional. I thought about how I shouldn't take my side projects so seriously and then in the same train of thought how I should quit my job to pursue them fully and if I truly enjoyed what I did, I wouldn't have to worry about the money. I thought about financial situation and how far and close I was to $4 million dollars. I thought about the insane commitment I'd say to someone, that I'd spent 22 years of my life trying to fit in and then the last 8 years being comfortable with who I am, that my delusions of grandeur and creation will likely come up short, that my goals may change, that I wasnt looking to absorb someone and was happy with the status quo but if they added to my life, I'd be unwaveringly faithful and excited to see the world through their eyes. I thought about how I wouldn't use dating apps, it'd have to be an approach. I thought about how the end doesn't concern me anymore, it's the middle parts where there's choices being made. I thought about how I'm done with games. I thought about how I hope my brother outgrows his feelings of inconveniencing people over his own comfort.  I thought about how recently my eyes get really watery again when I'm out in public spaces that aren't the gym almost like I'm going to cry. I thought about writing again. I thought about listening to Depression Cherry once more.

I think one of the primary allures of the movie on first watch is the unpredictability factor - not knowing where the tale of obsessive possession will go next for Nikki to snap and not exactly knowing just how unnerving she’ll become. Now on second watch knowing the outcomes of scenes and just trying to focus on the nuance more than haunting moments or thrills, the whole thing feels a little bit incoherent for the sake of bizarre shock rather than anything of meaning. The commentary on taking someone’s autonomy is existent with Bear’s character, but not to the exact extent of depth everyone claims. To me, Bear’s less a symbol of desperate incel men in the dating pools today, but if anything more so a plot device used to constantly be an idiot in denial in order for the story to further spiral into insanity. Maybe he’s selfish and too desperate for love, but he’s also very unrealistically cowardly to sit there submissively instead of trying to do something to get himself out of clear danger. No one’s that desperate for love. I can’t suspend my disbelief I’m sorry. There’s obviously the argument that this isn’t meant to be grounded in a natural reality since it’s in a sense of supernatural horror, but the magic of the horror genre is that it can take these seismic elements and ground them in metaphorical messages we can relate to. Bear just doesn’t really start to scratch that itch for me as far as realistic characters go. Neither does Nikki of being held captive under the wish. Most  of it seems less like an attempt at commentary but more like stitching jarring possessive characters choices together in order to shock the audience. While some of her characters choices under the willow make sense as someone purposely manipulative or volatile in order to show her obsessive love traits, there’s also many moments where that consistency breaks and Nikki suddenly acts out purely for the sake of being disturbing rather than it being a ploy around Bear. The personality was a thrilling experience to see on first watch with it keeping you on your toes, but now it just feels a bit goofy and ruining the attempt at any sort of genuine interest towards meaningful dialogue. The conversations end at him breaking the willow.

Add Nikki’s moves to Fortnite, 6.99 for the jitter in the corner emote It’s hard to give this an unbiased review with the discussion this provoked in culture, but I think people’s excitement about showing how men don’t value women’s autonomy is making them not see how this movie doesn’t say or do a whole lot else. Essentially we are starting with the premise of “what if pygmalion’s statue had some personality beforehand mixed with monkey paw antics”. It’s not a terrible idea but having the film be wholly in bears perspective loses most, if not all of the horror of Nikki’s side and diminishes any message trying to be put across. I get the idea, it was always superficial to him, so anytime she deviates from his ideal partner persona he starts being like “why am I here” only to be comforted by the touch and reassurance he bought and paid for. The idea that she is is fully under his control with no autonomy is mainly seen from his side (which doesn’t get talked enough about regarding the lacanian mirror philosophy of how she reflects bear back himself). And these ideas work fine but when here will the kernel of the movie be sprung: you can be a huge loser coward but don’t let being so pussillanimous hurt others. The conversation about this movie ends with “even the nice guys will rape you” which while true, isn’t going as far as the movie is even letting you step. We see bears cowardice and fear throughout the movie, and by only being able to judge what we see, he’s probably internalized some toxic masculinity from Ian if not also just from existence. Nikki doesn’t get possessed by any spirit, she gets possessed by bears spirit (maybe why you only get one wish) which is full of loser cowardice and will grovel at any push back to try to fix his mistakes. Obviously he gets worse as the movie goes on and he’s rightfully criticized and called a rapist but we need to interrogate why he did this and why he acted this way. He’s a person who wanted someone to love him. That’s not a crazy wish, I doubt even the most hardcore incel could claim they never wished to be loved nor the most attractive person in the world. It’s not a sin to want to ignore the rough parts of developing a relationship. We don’t know the backstory besides a few small fragments of any of the main crew which hurts everyone’s personhood and leads to a lot of flat moments from a filmmaking and thematic perspective; but what we can parse is that Nikki is nice, wants to write, and doesn’t like a high school nickname and that bear is indecisive and a coward. We aren’t going off a lot here. The “did she like him before the wish or not debate” is pointless because they both are withholding their honest feelings to each other. Bear is guessing because he’s a loser and can’t talk about his feelings while Nikki says she’s famously hard to read if she crushes on someone or not. There’s no fault on Bear for wishing she loved him in a normal seeming world where magic hasn’t shown to him to be real. Where we can criticize him though, is for his main trait through the movie of being a coward. This man is not in touch with himself, he said during the beginning monologue that Nikki was the first person he really felt he could open up to due to her being the only nice person when he moved there and couldn’t shake his feelings just from that. Buddy, go talk to a normal non fratty guy over beers and figure your shit out. You don’t need to wish and rape a mirror version of yourself who only gives into your worst desires as those consequences escalate. I would list the cowardice on display but then I’m citing the whole movie. I would give Obsession 2.5 out of 5 stars . Overall, I found the movie to be pretty strange, and while I thought the basic concept was interesting, I did not think the way the story played out worked very well. The idea behind the movie had a lot of potential and could have made for a really interesting psychological story, but I felt that the execution made the movie confusing and, at times, difficult to take seriously.One of my biggest problems was the story. I thought the plot had some interesting ideas, but the way everything developed felt somewhat forced and unrealistic. Instead of building tension naturally, some of the events felt like they were happening simply to move the story forward. I also felt that certain parts of the movie could have been developed more because the characters' decisions did not always make sense to me.The acting was okay overall, but it was not something that stood out to me. Watching something this psychological and gory at school probably wasn’t the smartest idea, but somehow being surrounded by my friends made the whole experience even better. Every disturbing moment became ten times funnier because of our reactions. From a horror lover’s perspective, I really enjoyed the overall plot. There was something genuinely smart about the way everything unfolded, and I liked that it wasn’t just relying on gore for the sake of being gory. The psychological side made it much more interesting, especially when you start questioning what’s actually happening and where things are going. That being said, the movie definitely felt a little too fast. I think some scenes could have been given more time to breathe, especially the moments that were building tension or developing the story. I wanted to sit with certain ideas a little longer instead of immediately being thrown into the next thing. Still, the combination of psychological horror, gore, disturbing moments, and the absolutely chaotic experience of watching it with friends made this such a fun watch. Definitely the kind of horror movie that becomes even better when you’re sitting next to your friends trying not to scream while also laughing at each other. Would I watch it again? Probably. Would I recommend watching it at school with your friends? Absolutely not… but also absolutely yes😭

Obsessão é um filme eu não entendo como o pessoal fala que é ruim, o único motivo plausível pra mim por pessoal não gostar é só questão de opinião mesmo, por que devemos concordar que o filme é muito bem feito. A fotografia é muito bonita e consegue criar uma sensação constante de desconforto, usando bem a iluminação e os enquadramentos para acompanhar o clima cada vez mais intenso da história. A trilha sonora talvez seja uma das melhores que eu já vi, principalmente pelo fato de tocar forever no final mas tirando isso as outras músicas também merece muito destaque. Ela ajuda bastante a construir a tensão e, em vários momentos, consegue deixar cenas comuns muito mais inquietantes. É aquele tipo de trilha que realmente contribui para a experiência do filme, em vez de simplesmente estar ali no fundo. A atuação da Inde Navarrette foi outro ponto que gostei bastante. Ela consegue transmitir muito bem as emoções da personagem, principalmente nos momentos em que a situação começa a fugir do controle. Para mim, é uma das melhores coisas do filme. Apesar disso, acho que o roteiro poderia desenvolver algumas situações e personagens um pouco melhor. Em certos momentos, senti que o filme poderia ir mais fundo nas ideias que apresenta, e o ritmo também oscila um pouco. Outro ponto que eu não gostei no filme é uma cena específica que o Ian deseja 1 bilhão de dólares e começa a cair rios de dinheiro, eu simplesmente odiei essa cena, pra mim acabou com clima da cena, considerando que o filme tava quase no final. Mesmo com esses problemas, Obsessão funciona muito bem como um suspense psicológico, principalmente por sua estética, sua trilha sonora e pela atuação da Inde Navarrette.
